questions.question: What does a triangular traffic sign with a red border signify?
options: Mandatory / Regulatory Sign
Cautionary / Warning Sign
Informative / Facility Sign
Speed Limit Enforcement Sign
questions.explanation: Triangular signs with red borders are cautionary signs warning the driver of potential road hazards or changes ahead.

questions.question: What does an octagonal red sign with white lettering indicate?
options: Yield to traffic
No Parking
Stop
Dead End Ahead
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign is uniquely reserved worldwide for the 'STOP' sign so drivers can recognize it even when covered in dust or snow.

questions.question: What does an inverted (upside down) triangular sign mean?
options: Give Way / Yield to traffic
Compulsory Turn Right
Pedestrian Crossing
Overtaking Permitted
questions.explanation: An inverted triangle is the 'Give Way' sign, mandating that you yield right of way to vehicles on the major road.

questions.question: A circular sign with a blue background and a diagonal red line across an electric horn means:
options: Compulsory sound horn
Horn prohibited (Silence Zone)
No entry for noisy vehicles
Railway crossing ahead
questions.explanation: A horn symbol crossed with a red slash indicates a Silence Zone near hospitals, educational institutions, and courts where honking is illegal.

questions.question: What is the key difference between 'No Parking' and 'No Stopping' signs?
options: There is no difference; both mean the same
In 'No Parking', you can briefly halt to drop or pick up passengers; in 'No Stopping', you cannot halt at all
'No Parking' applies to two-wheelers only
'No Stopping' applies only during night hours
questions.explanation: 'No Parking' (single red diagonal slash) allows momentary passenger boarding/alighting. 'No Stopping' (red 'X' cross) strictly prohibits even momentary halting.

questions.question: A circular sign with a red border containing the numeral '50' indicates:
options: Minimum speed is 50 km/h
Maximum speed limit is 50 km/h
Highway number 50 ahead
Next petrol station is 50 km away
questions.explanation: Numbers enclosed within a red circular ring denote maximum statutory speed limits for that road sector.

questions.question: When approaching an un-controlled pedestrian crossing where people are waiting to cross, you must:
options: Sound horn repeatedly and speed up
Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping
Stop before the zebra crossing line and wait until pedestrians have safely crossed
Flash your headlights to tell them to back away
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have absolute legal right of way at all pedestrian zebra crossings.

questions.question: From which side are you legally required to overtake a vehicle in India?
options: From the left side only
From the right side of the vehicle being overtaken
From whichever side has more clearance
Overtaking is completely banned on all Indian roads
questions.explanation: Under the Rules of the Road Regulations, drivers must overtake leading vehicles from their right side.

questions.question: When an emergency ambulance or fire brigade vehicle approaches from behind with sirens active, you must:
options: Maintain your current speed and lane
Accelerate quickly to stay ahead of the emergency vehicle
Immediately draw to the left side of the road and come to a stop to give free passage
Brake abruptly in the middle of your lane
questions.explanation: Section 194E of the Motor Vehicles Act makes obstructing emergency vehicles a severe offence punishable by up to ₹10,000 fine and/or 6 months imprisonment.

questions.question: Who has the right of way at a traffic rotary or roundabout?
options: Vehicles entering the roundabout from the left
Vehicles already circulating inside the roundabout on your right
The fastest moving vehicle
Heavy vehicles and buses always take precedence
questions.explanation: Traffic already circulating inside the rotary has precedence over vehicles waiting to enter the roundabout.

questions.question: Overtaking is strictly prohibited in which of the following circumstances?
options: On straight multi-lane expressways
On narrow bridges, blind curves, steep hilltops, and near pedestrian crossings
During clear daytime weather
When the vehicle ahead is moving at 40 km/h
questions.explanation: Overtaking on blind corners, narrow bridges, or pedestrian crossings is extremely dangerous due to zero sight distance.

questions.question: What is the maximum validity period of a Learner's Licence issued in India?
options: 30 days
3 months
6 months
1 year
questions.explanation: Under the Motor Vehicles Act, a Learner's Licence is valid for exactly 6 months throughout the territory of India.

questions.question: After obtaining a Learner's Licence, after how many days can you apply for a permanent Driving Licence test?
options: Immediately on the next day
After a mandatory waiting period of 30 days
After 90 days only
After 6 months
questions.explanation: An applicant must hold a valid Learner's Licence for at least 30 days before appearing for the permanent Driving Licence driving skill test.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal light at an intersection means:
options: The traffic signal is permanently broken; ignore it
Come to a complete stop, look in both directions, and proceed only when the road is completely clear
Slow down to 20 km/h and proceed without stopping
Road is permanently closed ahead
questions.explanation: A flashing red light equates to a 'STOP' sign: halt completely, yield to any cross traffic, and proceed only when clear.

questions.question: What does a continuous solid single white or yellow line along the center of the road signify?
options: You may overtake at any time
Crossing or straddling the line to overtake is strictly prohibited
The road is one-way only
Parking is permitted along the line
questions.explanation: A solid unbroken center line acts as a legal barrier: you must not cross or straddle it to overtake or make U-turns.

questions.question: What is the legal permissible Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) limit for driving a motor vehicle in India?
options: 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood
50 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood
100 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood
Zero alcohol tolerance for all commercial drivers, and max 30 mg/100ml for private drivers
questions.explanation: Under Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act, blood alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml blood (or any alcohol for commercial drivers) is punishable by heavy fines and imprisonment.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to obtain a Learner's Licence for a 50cc gearless motorcycle (MCWOG)?
options: 14 years
16 years (with written consent of parent or legal guardian)
18 years
21 years
questions.explanation: Section 4 of the Motor Vehicles Act allows individuals aged 16 and above to drive a motorcycle without gear up to 50cc with parental/guardian written consent.

questions.question: What is the mandatory safe following distance rule recommended when driving behind another vehicle at highway speeds?
options: 1 vehicle length at all speeds
The 'Two-Second Rule' under dry conditions (increased to 4 seconds in wet or foggy conditions)
5 meters strictly
Keep as close as possible to reduce wind drag
questions.explanation: The 'Two-Second Rule' guarantees adequate reaction and braking distance to prevent rear-end collisions.

questions.question: When driving a two-wheeler, who is legally required to wear a certified ISI / BIS protective safety helmet?
options: Only the rider / driver
Both the rider and the pillion passenger (except Sikhs wearing a turban)
Only when riding on national expressways
Helmets are optional inside municipal city limits
questions.explanation: Section 129 of the MV Act mandates certified protective headgear for both rider and pillion passenger.

questions.question: Using a handheld mobile phone while driving is permitted:
options: Only when stopped at a red traffic light
Only when driving below 30 km/h in residential zones
Never; using a handheld mobile phone while driving is illegal and a leading cause of fatal distraction
Whenever receiving urgent family phone calls
questions.explanation: Section 184(c) prohibits operating handheld mobile communication devices while driving, punishable with fines up to ₹5,000.
